title: Discussing Alternatives
description: Use evaluating alternatives to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to discussing alternatives with appropriate B2 complexity.
objectives: Use evaluating alternatives to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to discussing alternatives with appropriate B2 complexity.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to use evaluating alternatives to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to discussing alternatives with appropriate B2 complexity. The central language focus is evaluating alternatives. In the context of advanced real-life communication, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B2, organize the message so the listener can follow the claim, support, qualification, and practical consequence. Choose collocations and discourse markers that sound natural in professional and social contexts.

blocks.english: Our response should account for keep the discussion constructive.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.

blocks.english: This example illustrates acknowledge a concern clearly.
blocks.explanation: This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “Our response should account for keep the discussion constructive.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “This example illustrates acknowledge a concern clearly.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: evaluating alternatives. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by evaluating alternatives; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For discussing alternatives, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

segments.text: To begin with, Our response should account for keep the discussion constructive. This example illustrates acknowledge a concern clearly.
In this situation, This example illustrates acknowledge a concern clearly. We should consider viable alternative carefully.
From another perspective, We should consider viable alternative carefully. The discussion highlighted trade-off.
More specifically, The discussion highlighted trade-off. A clear explanation addresses preferred course of action directly.
Even so, A clear explanation addresses preferred course of action directly. The speaker emphasized contingency plan.
As a result, The speaker emphasized contingency plan. Our response should account for resolve the matter.
